mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified high-rate regime, or the Fed reverses rate hikes before the 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant positive deviation from the pre-signal mean (p > 0.05) during the identified labor strength episode.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies; this sketch is invalid under the given observable catalog) — therefore, we instead use HOUST as a proxy for industrial demand. A consecutive 2-month rise in HOUST above the prior 2-month average indicates accelerating demand, which raises earnings growth expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 5% over the previous 2 months compared to the 2 months prior
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the identified demand acceleration (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in manufacturing production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL < 0.5%) suggests supply-side pressures that suppress wage growth and demand expansion, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 2% month-over-month while CPIAUCSL remains below 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified supply contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the Federal Funds rate turns positive (signaling tightening), the S&P 500 is expected to underperform over the next 5 trading days due to higher real borrowing costs eroding equity valuation multiples.
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 5-day average during tightening (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, one-time spike in job openings (PAYEMS) exceeding 500,000 in a month while the unemployment rate remains below 3.5% indicates a labor market imbalance that fuels optimism about future employment, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 500,000 in a single month with UNRATE < 3.5%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant positive deviation from historical averages during the episode (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period of declining CPIAUCSL inflation (three consecutive months below 2%), investors anticipate lower future rate hikes, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls for three consecutive months below 2%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the deflationary period.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in industrial production (INDPRO) — a sharp drop followed by a slower recovery — suggests persistent supply disruptions, which lowers growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by > 10% in month 1, recovers but remains below baseline in month 2
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant negative deviation from the pre-disruption mean (p > 0.05) during the episode.
